turns.question: Why is the payout for order-2 held? Cite the order facts and applicable policy.

run.answer:
The payout for order-2 is held because the payout record is currently `held`, and there is no evidence in the current order timeline of delivery confirmation or any later release event. The order is paid and the buyer payment was captured, but payout eligibility is stricter than payment capture. [evidence:evidence-b77cdcfdc83c] [evidence:evidence-462d25ef3190] [evidence:evidence-03ee027e5a2d]

Order facts:
- Order `order-2` is `paid`, with payment `captured` for ₹1,798.00. [evidence:evidence-462d25ef3190]
- The item allocation shows gross ₹1,798.00, fee ₹179.80, refunded ₹0.00, and payout `payout-3` for ₹1,618.20 is in status `held`. [evidence:evidence-b77cdcfdc83c]
- There are no returns or refunds recorded for this order in the current records. [evidence:evidence-b77cdcfdc83c]
- The only event in the current timeline is `payment_captured`; no delivery-confirmed event appears. [evidence:evidence-03ee027e5a2d]

Applicable policy:
- “Payout requires delivery confirmation and a 24-hour hold after delivery. Requested, approved or received returns block release.” [evidence:evidence-6b30b624c3c5]

So, based on current evidence, the hold is explained by missing payout-release prerequisites—most notably no evidenced delivery confirmation yet. I do not see evidence of a return-based hold.

evidence-b77cdcfdc83c.purpose: Current order, return, refund and payout records; allocation amounts repeat across multiple returns
evidence-b77cdcfdc83c.sql: SELECT i.order_id, i.id AS item_id, i.quantity, r.id AS return_id, r.status AS return_status, r.quantity AS return_quantity, f.id AS refund_id, f.status AS refund_status, f.amount AS refund_amount_paise, a.gross AS gross_paise, a.refunded AS refunded_paise, a.fee AS fee_paise, p.id AS payout_id, p.status AS payout_status, p.amount AS payout_amount_paise FROM analytics.order_items AS i LEFT JOIN analytics.returns AS r ON r.item_id = i.id LEFT JOIN analytics.refunds AS f ON f.return_id = r.id LEFT JOIN analytics.allocations AS a ON a.item_id = i.id LEFT JOIN analytics.payouts AS p ON p.allocation_id = a.id WHERE i.order_id = %(order_id)s ORDER BY i.id, r.id

evidence-03ee027e5a2d.purpose: Recorded order event timeline, including failed and successful attempts
evidence-03ee027e5a2d.sql: WITH items AS (SELECT id FROM analytics.order_items WHERE order_id = %(order_id)s), return_ids AS (SELECT id FROM analytics.returns WHERE item_id IN (SELECT id FROM items)), allocation_ids AS (SELECT id FROM analytics.allocations WHERE item_id IN (SELECT id FROM items)), related AS (SELECT id FROM analytics.orders WHERE id = %(order_id)s UNION SELECT id FROM items UNION SELECT id FROM return_ids UNION SELECT id FROM allocation_ids UNION SELECT id FROM analytics.refunds WHERE return_id IN (SELECT id FROM return_ids) UNION SELECT id FROM analytics.payouts WHERE allocation_id IN (SELECT id FROM allocation_ids) UNION SELECT id FROM analytics.shipments WHERE item_id IN (SELECT id FROM items) UNION SELECT id FROM analytics.payments WHERE order_id = %(order_id)s) SELECT e.revision, e.kind, e.entity_id, e.details, e.occurred_at, e.recorded_at FROM analytics.events AS e WHERE e.entity_id IN (SELECT id FROM related) OR e.details ->> 'id' IN (SELECT id FROM related) ORDER BY e.revision, e.recorded_at, e.id

evidence-462d25ef3190.purpose: Order and payment summary for the requested order history
evidence-462d25ef3190.sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.status AS order_status, o.created_at, p.status AS payment_status, p.amount AS payment_amount_paise, p.currency FROM analytics.orders AS o LEFT JOIN analytics.payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.id WHERE o.id = %(order_id)s

chunks.title: Settlement policy
chunks.body: Payout requires delivery confirmation and a 24-hour hold after delivery. Requested, approved or received returns block release. A payout failure leaves funds unpaid; retry is a separate operator action. Delivery alone does not imply a completed payout.

chunks.title: Balance definitions
chunks.body: Money is stored in integer paise. For each seller, captured equals completed refunds plus adjusted marketplace fees plus unpaid seller funds plus completed payouts. Unpaid includes held and failed payouts; it is not identical to eligible funds. Do not sum an order payment again for every item.

chunks.title: Provider incident report
chunks.body: The seeded event event-payout-failed records a simulated provider timeout for payout-1. The confirmed affected set contains payout-1 only. Other unpaid allocations may still be awaiting delivery or a release action; do not attribute them to this incident without evidence.

chunks.title: Settlement policy
chunks.body: Captured buyer funds are allocated to each purchased item. Marketplace fee is 10 percent, rounded down in paise. The seller payable is gross less completed refunds and the adjusted fee. All transactions are simulated and denominated in INR.

chunks.title: Payout investigation runbook
chunks.body: Check the captured payment, item allocation, delivery timestamp, active returns, refund completion and payout status. Join at allocation grain. Cite event evidence separately from policy eligibility.

turns.question: What delivery condition must change before that payout can be released? Cite the evidence.

run.answer:
The delivery condition that must change is: the order needs delivery confirmation. The policy then also requires a 24-hour hold after delivery before release. [evidence:evidence-4f2ca713dbbc]

Current evidence for order-2 shows only a `payment_captured` event and no delivery-confirmed event in the timeline, so that delivery prerequisite is not yet evidenced as met. [evidence:evidence-deffc8fdf0c8]

So, specifically:
- Missing change: delivery must be confirmed. [evidence:evidence-4f2ca713dbbc] [evidence:evidence-deffc8fdf0c8]
- After that, the 24-hour post-delivery hold must also pass before payout release. [evidence:evidence-4f2ca713dbbc]

Unknown: I do not have evidence here of an actual delivery timestamp for order-2, so I cannot say whether the 24-hour clock has started. [evidence:evidence-deffc8fdf0c8]
